templates.description_en: Source-based adaptation of OpenEMR 8.4.1 for fictitious-patient testing. SOAP is the core note; optional sections are completed only when relevant and assessed. No findings, answers or dates are prefilled. Physical Exam records comments against the native examination lines without preselecting normal findings. This is not a claim of clinical validation, an exhaustive medical protocol or a clearance certificate.
templates.description_es: Adaptación basada en OpenEMR 8.4.1 para pruebas con pacientes ficticios. SOAP es la nota principal; las secciones opcionales se completan cuando corresponden y se evaluaron. No se precargan hallazgos, respuestas ni fechas. Physical Exam registra comentarios sobre las líneas del examen original sin marcar normalidad. No implica validación clínica, un protocolo médico exhaustivo ni un certificado de aptitud.

templates.description_en: Documentation adapted from public federal forms and the OpenEMR SOAP form. Complete only what was asked or assessed. Blank means not recorded; no answers or normal findings are preselected. For fictional-patient testing only. It is not a validated diagnostic instrument or a treatment consent.
templates.description_es: Registro adaptado de formularios federales públicos y del formulario SOAP de OpenEMR. Complete solo lo preguntado o evaluado. En blanco significa no registrado; no se preseleccionan respuestas ni hallazgos normales. Solo para pruebas con pacientes ficticios. No es un instrumento diagnóstico validado ni un consentimiento de tratamiento.

licensing_notes.note: IHS permits document reproduction unless otherwise stated; images and third-party content have separate restrictions. This adaptation uses textual field concepts and original layout, with no copied logos or images.

SF603 is a federal government form currently listed in the GSA library, revision 10/1975. Only clinical documentation concepts are adapted; no agency insignia, commercial code catalog or source artwork is included.
OpenEMR upstream source is GPL-licensed; the pinned source and LICENSE are preserved alongside this catalog. SOAP uses the four original OpenEMR field concepts.

adaptation_notes: All IHS medical-history questions, condition groups, wellbeing/safety questions, allergy choices, six medication rows and clinician notes are represented. Patient name, date of birth and record number come from the linked patient rather than duplicate answer fields.

Original yes/no questions and individual checklist choices are represented as optional yes/no/unknown selects without defaults. Unknown is an explicit adaptation; an omitted answer is not a negative answer.

The two wellbeing questions retain their original frequency choices. No score, cutoff, diagnosis or claim of instrument validation is calculated. Spanish wording is an independent aid, not an authorized or validated instrument translation.
Condition details retain the original request for dates and description; grouped source conditions remain grouped and are not converted into confirmed diagnoses.
The source's sex-gated reproductive heading is adapted to 'answer when applicable'; no sex-based response is inferred.

The IHS blanket consent paragraph and patient/provider signature lines are not reproduced as attestations. This catalog does not collect consent or simulate a legal signature. Authenticated reviewer/finalizer identity and timestamps are recorded by the application outside answers.
SF603 military rank, agency/branch, separation, dental readiness classifications, race and obsolete periodontal classifications are omitted. Periodontal findings remain free text for the clinician.

Tooth chart data remains outside answers in teeth[{number,condition,treatment}], with tooth_notation='universal' or 'fdi'. No diagram artwork is copied. Current observations and treatments are entered by the clinician; unselected teeth do not mean normal.
Requiring SOAP assessment and plan to finalize is this pilot's documentation policy, not an IHS/GSA legal requirement. The remainder stays optional for testing.

templates.description_en: Source-based subset of OpenEMR 8.4.1 Eye Exam for fictitious-patient testing. OD means right eye and OS means left eye. Refraction and acuity retain their examination context. Optional examination sections remain blank unless performed. One current spectacle pair and one impression/plan are represented. This adaptation has not been clinically validated and does not reproduce every native module workflow.
templates.description_es: Subconjunto basado en Eye Exam de OpenEMR 8.4.1 para pruebas con pacientes ficticios. OD significa ojo derecho y OS ojo izquierdo. La refracción y la agudeza conservan su contexto de medición. Las secciones opcionales quedan vacías si no se realizan. Se representa un par de anteojos actuales y una impresión/plan. Esta adaptación no tiene validación clínica ni reproduce todos los flujos del módulo original.

licensing_notes.note: The source states 'AUTHORIZED FOR LOCAL REPRODUCTION'. The adaptation uses textual documentation fields and its own layout, without logos, military identifiers or a copied signature block.

adaptation_notes: All clinical request, report, record-review, examination, telemedicine, facility/service, register and ward sections are represented. Linked patient identity supplies name, patient identifier, date of birth and other available demographics.
The military sponsor relationship/name/SSN and rank/grade block is omitted as inapplicable to this community-clinic pilot. No SSN is requested.

Doctor/consultant signature lines are not simulated. Requesting-provider text is descriptive only; authenticated author/finalizer identity and timestamps are recorded outside answers by the application. A stated professional title is not license verification.
Yes/no questions add an explicit unknown option. No answer or consultation urgency is preselected. Blank means not recorded rather than no.

The report label clarifies findings, opinion and recommendations as supported by the IHS consultation documentation guidance; no clinical clearance algorithm or generic cleared/not-cleared decision is introduced.
Source bedside and on-call placement/availability markers are retained as independent optional answers. They do not imply that these care settings are offered by the event.

Historical version-1 clearance decisions must remain unchanged and readable in their original version. This version is a consultation document, not a retrospective reinterpretation of those decisions.
Requiring a consultation report to finalize is the pilot's documentation policy. Other source fields remain optional for fictional-patient testing.
Spanish labels are an independent translation aid and are not an official GSA translation.
